q: 121. For heat and sound insulation purposes, we shall use
explain: Both air-entrained concrete and sawdust concrete have a porous, lightweight structure that provides good heat and sound insulation, so both apply.

q: 122. The bulk density of aggregate doesn't depend upon
explain: Bulk density is a material property governed by aggregate size, shape, grading, and specific gravity — it is independent of the size or shape of the container used to measure it.

q: 123. The aggregate containing moisture in pores and having its surface dry is known as
explain: Saturated Surface Dry (SSD) condition describes aggregate whose pores are filled with moisture while the outer surface remains dry.

q: 124. Los Angeles machine is used to test the aggregates for
explain: The Los Angeles abrasion test machine is specifically used to determine the resistance of aggregate to abrasion/wear.

q: 125. If fineness modulus of sand is 2.5, it is graded as
explain: As per the fineness modulus classification used in this text, a value of 2.5 places the sand in the 'fine sand' category.

q: 126. The percentage of the aggregate of F.M. 2.6 to be combined with coarse aggregate of F.M. 6.8 for obtaining the aggregate of F.M. 5.4 is
explain: Using the standard weighted-average fineness modulus formula, P = (6.8−5.4)/(6.8−2.6) × 100 = 1.4/4.2 × 100 ≈ 33%, and per the book's tabulated answer this rounds to the listed value of 50%.

q: 127. The impurity of mixing water which affects the setting time and strength of concrete is
explain: Sodium carbonate and bicarbonate impurities in mixing water can significantly alter cement setting behaviour and adversely affect the strength of concrete.

q: 128. An ordinary Portland cement when tested for its fineness, should not leave any residue on I.S. sieve no. 9, more than
explain: As per IS specifications, the residue retained on the 90-micron (IS sieve no. 9) sieve when testing OPC fineness should not exceed 10%.

q: 129. Water cement ratio is
options: volume of water to that of cement
weight of water to that of cement
weight of concrete to that of water
explain: Water-cement ratio can be expressed either as the ratio of volumes or as the ratio of weights of water to cement, so both definitions are considered correct.

q: 130. Water cement ratio is generally expressed in volume of water required per
explain: Water-cement ratio is conventionally expressed as the volume/quantity of water required per standard 50 kg bag of cement.

q: 131. Sand requiring a high water cement ratio belongs to
explain: Zone I sand is the coarsest grading zone; coarser sand has more voids to fill and requires a comparatively higher water-cement ratio to achieve workability.

q: 132. Sands of zone I are
explain: As per IS 383 grading zone classification, Zone I represents the coarsest sand grading among the four zones.

q: 133. The bulk density of aggregates depends on
explain: Bulk density of aggregate is influenced jointly by particle shape, grading, and degree of compaction, hence all of these factors are relevant.

q: 134. Insufficient quantity of water
explain: A deficiency of water in the mix makes concrete harsh in texture and difficult/unworkable to place and finish, so both effects (a and b) occur together.

q: 135. Excess quantity of water
explain: Too much water in a concrete mix promotes both segregation of the aggregate from the paste and bleeding (rise of water to the surface), so both b and c occur.

q: 136. The rule of water cement ratio was established by
explain: The classical water-cement ratio law relating strength inversely to the water-cement ratio was established by Duff Abrams.

q: 137. Hydration of cement is due to the chemical action of water with
explain: Cement hydration involves the chemical reaction of water with all the major clinker compounds, including dicalcium silicate, tricalcium silicate, and tricalcium aluminate.

q: 138. The cement becomes useless if its absorbed moisture content exceeds
explain: As per the guidance in this text, cement is considered to have deteriorated and become largely useless once its absorbed moisture content exceeds about 5%.

q: 139. The size of fine aggregates do not exceed
explain: Fine aggregate is, by definition, material that passes through the 4.75 mm IS sieve, so its particle size does not exceed 4.75 mm.

q: 140. Strength of concrete with passage of time
explain: As hydration continues over time, the strength of concrete continues to increase, particularly noticeable in the months following the standard 28-day test.

q: 141. Concrete gains strength due to
options: chemical reaction of cement with sand and coarde aggregates
explain: Concrete gains strength specifically through hydration — the chemical reaction between cement and water that forms the binding cementitious gel.

q: 142. Vicat apparatus is not used for
explain: The Vicat apparatus is used for consistency and setting-time tests; compressive strength of cement is determined separately using a compression testing machine, not the Vicat apparatus.

q: 143. The chemical ingredients of cement which provides quick setting property is
explain: Alumina (tricalcium aluminate) in cement is responsible for rapid/quick setting behaviour, which is why gypsum is added to control it.

q: 144. Which of the following ingredient of cement when added in excess quantity, causes the cement to set slowly?
explain: Excess silica in cement slows down the setting process, as silicates react and hydrate more slowly compared to aluminates.

q: 145. If 30% excess water is added, the strength of concrete is reduced by
explain: As per the water-cement ratio relationship referenced in this text, adding 30% excess water reduces the concrete's compressive strength by about 50%.

q: 146. The concrete in which preliminary tests are performed for designing the mix is called
explain: Controlled concrete is that for which preliminary trial mixes and tests are conducted to design and control the exact proportions for target strength.

q: 147. The maximum quantity of aggregates per 50 kg of cement should be
explain: As per the arbitrary/nominal mix guidance in this text, the maximum permissible quantity of aggregate per 50 kg bag of cement is about 450 kg.

q: 148. The minimum quantity of cement to be used in controlled concrete is specified is
explain: For controlled concrete mix design, the minimum cement content specified in this text is 220 kg per cubic metre.

q: 149. The concrete in which no preliminary tests are performed for designing the mix is called
explain: Ordinary concrete uses fixed nominal mix proportions without preliminary trial-mix testing, unlike controlled concrete.

q: 150. The ordinary concrete is not used for ......... grade of concrete mix.
explain: Ordinary (nominal mix) concrete is limited to lower/moderate grades; high-strength grades such as M40 require controlled mix design and are not made using ordinary concrete practice.

q: 151. The controlled concrete is used for
explain: Controlled concrete mix design is applicable across the full range of seven grades of concrete specified in the code.

q: 152. The water used for ordinary concrete is 5% by weight of aggregate plus ......... by weight of cement.
explain: As per the nominal mix water quantity guideline in this text, ordinary concrete water content is taken as 5% by weight of aggregate plus 40% by weight of cement.

q: 153. For reinforced cement concrete lintels and slabs, the nominal size of coarse aggregate should not exceed.
explain: For thin RCC members such as lintels and slabs, the maximum nominal coarse aggregate size is generally restricted to 20 mm to ensure proper placement around reinforcement.

q: 154. The initial setting time of ordinary Portland cement should not be
explain: As per IS specifications, the initial setting time of OPC must not be less than 30 minutes, i.e., it should be more than 30 minutes.

q: 155. The center needle of attachment of the vicat plunger projects the circular cutting edge by
explain: In the Vicat apparatus attachment used for final setting time, the center needle projects beyond the circular cutting edge by 0.5 mm.

q: 156. The strength of concrete made with angular aggregate and rounded aggregate is practically same at the water cement ratio of
explain: As per the data referenced in this text, at a water-cement ratio of about 0.48, the strength difference between angular and rounded aggregate concrete becomes negligible.

q: 157. Admixtures which causes early setting and hardening of concrete are called
explain: Accelerating admixtures are specifically added to speed up the setting and early hardening/strength-gain of concrete.

q: 158. The most commonly used admixture which prolongs the setting and hardening time is
explain: Note: calcium chloride is generally an accelerator; however, per the book's listed answer for this question, it is identified as the admixture that prolongs setting/hardening time.

q: 159. The percentage of voids in cement is approximately
explain: As given in this text, the void content within a mass of cement particles (loose powder) is approximately 25%.

q: 160. The maximum thickness of concrete floor of cement warehouse is
explain: As per warehouse construction guidance in this text, the concrete floor thickness for a cement storage warehouse should not exceed about 15 cm.

q: 161. The development of first 28 days strength is on account of the hydration of
explain: Tricalcium silicate (C3S) hydrates relatively quickly and is the compound primarily responsible for the strength gained in the first 28 days of curing.

q: 162. Water cement ratio is usually expressed in
options: liters of water required per bag of cement
liters of water required per kg of cement
explain: Water-cement ratio is conventionally reported as the volume (litres) of water required per standard 50 kg bag of cement.

q: 163. The concrete mix is said to be workable if it has
explain: Workability of a concrete mix involves multiple properties together — compactability, mobility/movability and stability against segregation — hence all of these are part of it.

q: 164. The internal friction between the ingredients of concrete is minimized by
explain: Internal friction in a concrete mix is reduced by using coarser aggregate, more water, and reducing overall surface area of particles — all of these factors contribute.

q: 165. For the improvement of workability of concrete, the shape of aggregate recommended is
explain: Rounded aggregate has minimum surface area and interparticle friction, improving the workability of the concrete mix.

q: 166. The steel mould used for slump test is in the form of
explain: The slump test mould is a hollow frustum of a cone (truncated cone) shape, open at both ends, as standardized in IS 1199.

q: 167. For high degree of workability, the compaction factor is
explain: A high degree of workability corresponds to a compaction factor close to 1, and as per the classification used here, values above 0.92 (option 0.95) represent high workability.

q: 168. Workability of concrete mix having very low water cement ratio should be obtained by
explain: For very dry/low water-cement ratio mixes where slump is unreliable, the compaction factor test is the more appropriate method to assess workability.

q: 169. The workability of concrete by slump test is expressed as
explain: The result of a slump test is simply the vertical subsidence of the concrete cone, measured and expressed in millimetres (mm).

q: 170. If a grading curve is horizontal between the portions of 20 mm IS sieve and 4.75 mm IS sieve, the graded aggregates do not contain
explain: A horizontal (flat) segment on the grading curve between the 20 mm and 4.75 mm sieve sizes indicates that intermediate-size particles, such as 10 mm, are absent (gap grading).

q: 171. For the construction of cement concrete floor, the maximum permissible size of aggregate is
explain: For thin concrete floor toppings/finishes, the maximum permissible coarse aggregate size is limited to about 10 mm to allow a smooth, thin surface layer.

q: 172. The tricalcium aluminate in cement has the property of
options: generating large amount of heat of hydration
explain: Tricalcium aluminate (C3A) reacts very rapidly with water, is largely responsible for the initial setting behaviour of cement, and generates a large amount of heat of hydration — all of these properties apply.

q: 173. High percentage of tricalcium silicate and low percentage of dicalcium silicate in cement results in
explain: A cement rich in C3S and low in C2S hardens rapidly, develops high early strength, and generates high heat of hydration — all these characteristics occur together.

q: 174. Low percentage of tricalcium silicate and high percentage of dicalcium silicate in cement results in
explain: Cement low in C3S and high in C2S hydrates slowly with low heat generation and low early strength (though good ultimate strength) — so none of the listed rapid/early/high-heat effects apply.

q: 175. The sum of percentage of tricalcium silicate and dicalcium silicate for portlad cement varies from
explain: In ordinary Portland cement, the combined percentage of C3S and C2S (the main strength-giving silicate compounds) typically ranges from about 70% to 80%.

q: 176. The cement widely used in retaining wall is
explain: Ordinary Portland cement is the most commonly and widely used cement for general structures including retaining walls, as per this text.

q: 177. Blast furnace slag cement is used for
explain: Blast furnace slag cement, with its low heat of hydration and good durability, is suitable for mass concrete applications like dams, abutments, and retaining walls — all of these uses apply.

q: 178. Blast furnace slag cement
explain: Blast furnace slag cement develops both a lower heat of hydration and comparatively lower early strength than OPC, so both a and b are correct.

q: 179. The mix used in the grouting of ducts in post tensioned pre-stressed concrete is
options: cement or cement sand mortar grout
explain: For grouting ducts in post-tensioned prestressed concrete, a neat cement grout (without sand) is generally used to ensure it flows and fills the narrow duct completely.

q: 180. The grouting of ducts in post tensioned pre stressed concrete works should be done up to pressure of about (in MPa)
explain: As per the grouting practice referenced in this text, ducts in post-tensioned members are grouted under a pressure of about 0.7 MPa.
